question: m12
q: Is electricity inflation running ahead of overall inflation?

transcript.answer:
Yes, by a wide margin. In **August 2026**, electricity prices were up **13.2%** on a year earlier. Overall CPI inflation was **4.0%**, so electricity is rising more than three times as fast.

**Annual change, Australia (ABS monthly CPI, original):**

| Month | Electricity | All groups CPI |
|---|---|---|
| Jun 2025 | −6.3% | 1.9% |
| Oct 2025 | 37.1% | 3.8% |
| Feb 2026 | 37.0% | 3.7% |
| Jun 2026 | 22.4% | 3.8% |
| Jul 2026 | 6.1% | 3.5% |
| Aug 2026 | 13.2% | 4.0% |

**What the numbers show:**
- **Electricity has outpaced overall inflation every month since July 2025.** Before that, electricity prices were falling year on year, as low as −13.2% in February 2025.
- **The peak was around 37%** in October 2025 and February 2026. Since then the rate has slowed a lot, down to 6.1% in July 2026, before rising again to 13.2% in August.
- **Big swings like these usually come from government energy bill rebates** starting, stopping or changing size, not just from changes in underlying tariffs. The CPI measures what households actually pay after rebates. So a rebate change can push the annual rate sharply up or down. The data doesn't show the cause directly, but the size and timing of these moves fit that pattern.

Overall inflation is also high: 4.0% in August 2026, above the RBA's 2–3% target band. Electricity is one of the things pushing it up.
